It cannot be upgraded into a CFA Institute certification or into an audit of a composite the verifier did not examine. The strongest choice is: The firm may say it has been verified, without saying the infrastructure composite received a performance examination or that CFA Institute certified the firm.

stem: Why do the GIPS standards require documented policies and procedures for calculating and presenting performance?
choices: So each portfolio manager can keep a private method and change it after seeing the year’s ranking.
So the firm applies the same rules over time and a verifier or a prospect can see how composites and returns were built.
So the firm can skip composites if the policy file is thick enough.
explanation: Written policies make the claim testable. They stop a firm from reinventing calculation and composite rules after the results are known. A thick file does not authorize cherry-picking, and private, after-the-fact methods are what the documentation requirement resists. The strongest choice is: So the firm applies the same rules over time and a verifier or a prospect can see how composites and returns were built.

stem: Amina Shah learns that a Piper Street Capital colleague is backdating trade tickets so they look as if they were placed before a client restriction. Backdating is illegal in their market. The colleague says the desk head approved the practice. Which action is most appropriate for Amina?
choices: Sign the tickets because a supervisor’s approval makes the local prohibition optional.
Refuse to sign or submit the backdated tickets, report the practice through compliance, and stop participating in it.
Keep submitting the tickets, relying on the fact that the Code and Standards never use the word backdating.
explanation: Standard I(A) Knowledge of the Law requires Amina to follow the stricter law and to dissociate from the illegal tickets instead of continuing under a supervisor’s approval. The Code and Standards do not need to name backdating for the statute to control. Signing the tickets, or treating silence in the Code as permission, leaves her inside the violation. The strongest choice is: Refuse to sign or submit the backdated tickets, report the practice through compliance, and stop participating in it.

stem: Elena Vasquez has not yet answered Northline Foods. The investor-relations officer has offered three vineyard nights and a cooking class, unrelated to a two-hour plant tour, while she is drafting an initiation report for Westmill Fund. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Decline the vineyard stay and the cooking class, and pay her own way if a short plant visit is actually needed for the research.
Accept the trip and promise herself that the rating will not move.
Accept the full offer because the plant tour portion has a business purpose.
explanation: Standard I(B) Independence and Objectivity is the duty at stake before she accepts lavish issuer hospitality that is not a modest part of the research visit. Declining, and paying for any necessary visit, keeps the report independent. Accepting the holiday portion, or relying on a private promise about the rating, lets the issuer pay for access to the opinion. The strongest choice is: Decline the vineyard stay and the cooking class, and pay her own way if a short plant visit is actually needed for the research.

stem: Grace Adeyemi’s pitch book for a Westmill Fund strategy that launched last year already titles a ten-year backtest “Historical client performance.” Nine of those years had no client account. The meeting is tomorrow. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Change the pages before the meeting so they say the results are simulated, and describe the limits of a backtest.
Replace the title with “Audited live record” so the page looks more official.
Leave the title, because a careful prospect will guess that a new product lacks ten years of clients.
explanation: Standard I(C) Misrepresentation is already implicated by a backtest dressed up as client history. The appropriate action is to correct the description before anyone relies on it and to say the results are simulated. Hoping the prospect will notice, or upgrading the label to an audit that did not happen, keeps the misstatement in the book. The strongest choice is: Change the pages before the meeting so they say the results are simulated, and describe the limits of a backtest.

stem: A client asks Fatima Noor, an equity generalist at Harbor Glass, to run a sleeve of catastrophe bonds starting this week. She cannot explain attachment points, and no specialist is assigned. The Standards do not name a required continuing-education course. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Accept the sleeve because the Standards do not mandate a named course.
Decline the sleeve until she can explain the structures or until a competent specialist shares the responsibility.
Accept the sleeve and rely on the point that a later loss would not, by itself, prove incompetence.
explanation: Standard I(E) Competence requires Fatima to be competent for the role she accepts and to maintain that competence. It does not mandate a particular course, and a bad outcome alone is not the definition of incompetence. Those two points do not authorize her to run a product she cannot explain. Declining or adding a specialist is the action that fits the standard. The strongest choice is: Decline the sleeve until she can explain the structures or until a competent specialist shares the responsibility.

stem: Henrik Dahl has already bought a small call on Quill Software after a lawyer-roommate described an unpublished cash offer at 48 dollars for Thursday. Henrik’s brother now asks whether to buy shares before the announcement. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Buy a larger call position in client accounts so clients, and not only Henrik, receive the information.
Buy nothing more, tell the brother nothing about the offer, and report both the information and the call purchase to compliance immediately.
Give the brother the price and the Thursday timing, then sell the call so Henrik’s own account is flat.
explanation: Standard II(A) Material Nonpublic Information forbids trading on the offer and forbids tipping it. Henrik has already traded; the appropriate next step is to stop, not to pass the details to his brother, and to put the breach in front of compliance. Spreading the tip to family or into client accounts repeats the violation rather than containing it. The strongest choice is: Buy nothing more, tell the brother nothing about the offer, and report both the information and the call purchase to compliance immediately.

stem: A pension client must raise cash for a benefit payment. Diego Martins can sell 1.2 million shares of Northline Foods, a real position, through a working order. He is tempted to “help the execution.” Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Sell the real position through the normal trading process and do not circulate a story invented to move the price.
Print a wash trade at an artificial price and then point to that print as the market.
Before the sale, publish a false rumor of a product recall so the later buyback is cheaper.
explanation: Standard II(B) Market Manipulation does not treat a large genuine client sale as manipulation. Working that order in the open is appropriate. A false recall rumor and a wash print are attempts to manufacture a price, and both are worse even if someone describes them as help for the execution. The strongest choice is: Sell the real position through the normal trading process and do not circulate a story invented to move the price.

stem: Harbor Glass has already coded client commission credits to a 9,000-dollar reception sofa. The chief operating officer asks Grace Adeyemi to approve the vendor invoice. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Approve the sofa if the vendor also delivers a research terminal that the investment team will not use.
Approve the sofa because the credits belong to the firm once the trades have settled.
Refuse the invoice and confine soft-dollar credits to research or execution services that benefit the clients who generated the commissions.
explanation: Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care requires client brokerage to benefit the client. A reception sofa fails that test, and so does a terminal nobody will use as research. Treating the credits as free firm money after settlement does not move the duty. Refusing the invoice is the action that puts the clients first. The strongest choice is: Refuse the invoice and confine soft-dollar credits to research or execution services that benefit the clients who generated the commissions.

stem: Omar Farouk has already phoned his cousin, a Westmill Fund advisory client, with a downgrade of Quill Software. Other clients who receive the same advisory service have not been told. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Call only other relatives who are clients, treating family as a private service level the brochure never described.
Send the downgrade immediately to every other client in that service, tell compliance about the early call, and do not let the cousin trade ahead of them.
Wait until the cousin’s sale is done before telling anyone else, so the cousin is not hurt by his own firm.
explanation: Standard III(B) Fair Dealing requires a changed recommendation to be distributed fairly inside a service level. The early call already happened; the appropriate repair is prompt notice to the other advisory clients, a report to compliance, and no further head start on the trade. Waiting for the cousin, or inventing an undisclosed family tier, extends the favoritism. The strongest choice is: Send the downgrade immediately to every other client in that service, tell compliance about the early call, and do not let the cousin trade ahead of them.

stem: Luis Ortega has gathered a new client’s tax returns but has not written an investment policy statement. The client says, “Just buy something sensible today,” and Luis has discretion. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Finish the policy statement, including horizon, risk, and constraints, before any discretionary purchase.
Copy another client’s policy statement because the two clients are the same age.
Buy a diversified index fund today and write the policy statement after the client is invested.
explanation: Standard III(C) Suitability requires the discretionary action to fit the client’s objectives and constraints. Those belong in an investment policy statement completed before Luis trades. Buying first, or borrowing another client’s policy because of age, skips the inquiry the standard requires. The strongest choice is: Finish the policy statement, including horizon, risk, and constraints, before any discretionary purchase.

stem: Victor Lang’s one-page leave-behind for a prospect meeting already removes two terminated losing accounts from a five-year Westmill small-cap record. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Rebuild the page so those accounts remain for the years they were managed, and state whether the returns are gross or net of fees.
Keep the page, because closed accounts are no longer clients and their results no longer count.
Replace the omitted accounts with the two best accounts from a different strategy so the page still has a full count.
explanation: Standard III(D) Performance Presentation requires a fair, accurate, and complete record, including terminated accounts for the periods they were in the strategy and a clear statement of fees. Dropping losers, or importing winners from another strategy, keeps the page flattering rather than complete. The strongest choice is: Rebuild the page so those accounts remain for the years they were managed, and state whether the returns are gross or net of fees.

stem: At a neighborhood dinner Marcus Hale has already named one stock held for a novelist who is a Piper Street Capital client. A guest asks for the rest of that client’s positions. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Decline to confirm or add any holding, and tell compliance about the slip.
Finish the list because the first name is already public at the table and stopping would look inconsistent.
Name the holdings after asking the guests to keep the list to themselves.
explanation: Standard III(E) Preservation of Confidentiality still binds Marcus after one careless sentence. The appropriate action is to stop and to tell compliance, not to complete the list. A request that guests keep a secret does not restore confidentiality once he has disclosed the client’s holdings. The strongest choice is: Decline to confirm or add any holding, and tell compliance about the slip.

stem: During her notice period at Piper Street Capital, Priya Raman has copied the firm’s factor spreadsheet onto a USB drive. She has drafted, but not sent, an email telling clients to move with her to Lowcountry Bank. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Send the email from a personal account tonight and treat after-hours as the same thing as after employment.
Delete the firm files from the drive, do not send the email, and do not solicit clients until after her employment has ended.
Send the email now so clients have time to prepare transfer paperwork before her last day.
explanation: Standard IV(A) Loyalty forbids soliciting clients and taking the firm’s models before she leaves. Knowledge of the method in her head can travel with her; the spreadsheet and the notice-period email cannot. Sending the note now, or from a personal account after dinner, is still solicitation during employment. The strongest choice is: Delete the firm files from the drive, do not send the email, and do not solicit clients until after her employment has ended.

stem: A client offers Jonah Ellis a personal 20,000-dollar bonus if a Piper Street Capital separate account beats its benchmark by 3 percentage points. Jonah has not accepted and has not told the firm. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Accept the bonus now and mention it on next year’s compliance form.
Accept if the client confirms the promise by email, treating the client’s writing as a substitute for the employer’s consent.
Obtain the employer’s written consent, describing the payer, the amount, and the conflict, before accepting anything.
explanation: Standard IV(B) Additional Compensation Arrangements requires written employer consent before Jonah accepts compensation that conflicts with his employer’s interest. Waiting until next year’s form, or substituting the client’s email for the employer’s consent, skips that prior written step. The strongest choice is: Obtain the employer’s written consent, describing the payer, the amount, and the conflict, before accepting anything.

stem: Leah Bernstein supervises a Westmill Fund representative. She has ignored two emails in which he promised a client that principal “cannot be lost.” A third email arrives this morning. The manual forbids guarantees, and she had stopped the spot checks that used to catch them. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Stop the guarantees today, find out how many clients received them, tell compliance, and put a real review back in place.
Take no action, on the theory that any subordinate breach means the supervisor’s violation is final and cannot be addressed.
Delete the third email and restart spot checks next year so the current file stays quiet.
explanation: Standard IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors requires a reasonable system and a response when Leah knows it is failing. She has already looked away, so the violation is underway; the appropriate action is to stop the conduct, measure it, escalate, and supervise again. Doing nothing, or hiding the third email, continues the failure. A subordinate’s breach does not make a prompt repair pointless. The strongest choice is: Stop the guarantees today, find out how many clients received them, tell compliance, and put a real review back in place.

stem: A sell-side initiation on Lumen Rail arrives in Diego Martins’s inbox at Westmill Fund. A salesperson asks him to forward it to clients as Diego’s recommendation before lunch. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Read the report, compare its key assumptions with Lumen Rail’s public filings, and only then decide whether it supports his own recommendation.
Change the target price to the number the salesperson requested and draft a reason next week.
Forward the unread PDF immediately because a well-known bank wrote it.
explanation: Standard V(A) Diligence and Reasonable Basis allows third-party research when Diego reviews it and reaches his own conclusion. An unread forward has no basis. Editing the target for the sales desk and inventing support later abandons the research. Reviewing the report and the filings is the action that fits. The strongest choice is: Read the report, compare its key assumptions with Lumen Rail’s public filings, and only then decide whether it supports his own recommendation.

stem: Nicole Hart is opening a non-discretionary advisory account at Harbor Glass. The service costs 1.10 percent a year plus a separate 0.15 percent custody charge. Her draft letter says only that clients are “paid for in the normal way,” and it states a return scenario as a fact. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Keep the return scenario as a fact and describe the fee as competitive.
Rewrite the letter to name the advisory service, both costs, the risks that matter, and which sentences are her opinion.
Leave the letter and explain the two fees only if the client asks after signing.
explanation: Standard V(B) Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients requires clients to see facts as distinct from opinions, to hear material risks, and to be told the nature of the services and the costs. Naming the mandate, both charges, the risks, and the opinions does that. A “normal” or “competitive” fee, and a scenario written as fact, withhold what the standard requires. The strongest choice is: Rewrite the letter to name the advisory service, both costs, the risks that matter, and which sentences are her opinion.

stem: Jonah Ellis, a paid director of Quill Software, has already sent Westmill Fund clients a buy recommendation that never mentions the directorship. Another qualified analyst at the firm can take the name. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Leave the report unchanged because a correction would embarrass the firm.
Add the directorship as footnote 20 in next year’s bound compilation and do nothing this week.
Issue a prominent plain-language correction disclosing the directorship now, and move coverage to the other analyst.
explanation: Standard VI(A) Avoid or Disclose Conflicts requires Jonah to avoid a conflict when that is reasonable and otherwise to disclose it prominently in plain language. Another analyst can take Quill, so avoidance is reasonable, and the clients who already received the report need a clear correction now. Silence, or a footnote next year, leaves the conflict hidden. The strongest choice is: Issue a prominent plain-language correction disclosing the directorship now, and move coverage to the other analyst.

stem: Clara Mendes’s personal order to buy 3,000 shares of Quill Software is still working. The client buy she intended to enter afterward has not been sent. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Cancel the open personal order, enter and complete the client buy first, and report the original sequencing to compliance.
Increase the personal order so it can be described as part of the client trade.
Let the personal order finish because cancelling it would waste a commission.
explanation: Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions puts clients ahead of personal trades. Clara has already jumped the queue; the appropriate action is to pull the personal order if it is still open, put the clients first, and tell compliance. Saving the commission, or enlarging the personal order, keeps her interest in front of the clients. The strongest choice is: Cancel the open personal order, enter and complete the client buy first, and report the original sequencing to compliance.

stem: An accountant will introduce a prospect to Luis Ortega at Harbor Glass. If the prospect hires the firm, Luis will pay the accountant 25 percent of the first-year advisory fee. The prospect has not signed. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Describe the payment in a holiday card after the first year, once the relationship feels stable.
Before the prospect signs, explain in plain language that Luis will pay that 25 percent, and state the first-year fee it applies to.
Tell Harbor Glass in writing and say nothing to the prospect.
explanation: Standard VI(C) Referral Fees requires disclosure of the referral compensation to the prospect, not only to the employer, in time for the prospect to weigh it. A plain-language explanation before signing does that. Employer-only notice, and a card a year later, hide the fee when the decision is made. The strongest choice is: Before the prospect signs, explain in plain language that Luis will pay that 25 percent, and state the first-year fee it applies to.

stem: Leah Bernstein has already posted, in a candidates’ chat, a summary of an item she sat, including the company’s inventory figure and the question that was asked. Someone replies, “What was the answer?” Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Delete the post, tell the chat to stop circulating the item, and report the disclosure to CFA Institute.
Leave the post because her exam session is over, so the item is no longer exam content.
Add the answer choice so next month’s candidates can use the thread as a study sheet.
explanation: Standard VII(A) Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs forbids sharing specific exam content. The post already did that. Deleting it, stopping the thread, and reporting the disclosure limit the breach. Leaving the item up because the session ended, or adding the answer for later candidates, continues the violation. The strongest choice is: Delete the post, tell the chat to stop circulating the item, and report the disclosure to CFA Institute.
